valuation.method: Forward EPS x justified P/E. Listing is the NYSE common stock in USD (no ADR conversion). Base EPS is the FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance (about 12% growth excluding the 53rd week, on FY2025 adjusted EPS of about $5.93, so about $6.64), grown one year to FY2027 at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027). Bear 5% growth at 16x, base 10% growth at 18x, bull 15% growth at 20x. Information cutoff is the 2026-11-13 close; the Q4 FY2026 release scheduled for 2026-11-17 is a subsequent event and is not used.

bear.driver: Growth slows to mid-single digits; parks and streaming margin gains fade; market keeps a discount multiple

base.driver: Management's double-digit EPS growth framework is met; buybacks of about $9B a year support per-share growth

bull.driver: Experiences and streaming profit beat the framework; multiple re-rates toward the historical premium

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027 EPS of $7.30 the close of $118.97 implies 16.3x; on FY2026 EPS of $6.64 it implies 17.9x. The aggregate analyst mean of $126.79 implies about 17.4x base EPS, so the gap to the base case is mostly multiple, not EPS.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $7.30 (about 5.6%, or 6.1 pp of price return). A two-point EPS change at 18x moves it by about $36.
valuation.watch_metric: FY2027 adjusted EPS growth against the double-digit framework, with Experiences operating income growth and streaming operating margin as the drivers
valuation.next_disclosure: Q1 FY2027 earnings (expected around February 2027), where FY2027 guidance is tested; the FY2026 Q4 and full-year results released 2026-11-17 are a subsequent event to review in a later run

analyst_notes: Only two named analysts with dated calls could be verified from the sources reached: Steven Cahall (Wells Fargo) raised the target from $125 to $132 and kept Overweight on 2026-08-06, and Mike Hickey (Benchmark) reiterated Buy with a $115 target the same day. Neither source documents a 12-month horizon, so these calls stay in the timeline but are excluded from the weighted target. The aggregate mean of $126.79 across about 30 analysts includes many unnamed or undated targets, so it cannot be reconciled to named calls; the base case at $131.40 sits above the aggregate mean, and the gap is attributable to multiple (about 18x against an implied 17.4x) rather than a disputed EPS base.
